## Ghana Onset Data

We pull the date of onset from the Savannah, Ghana data to get the number of 
symptomatic cases, which we are using as a proxy for newly symptomatic YF cases

```{r ghana-parse-savannah-data}

# Country specific variables
country = "ghana"
region.pop = 653266
vacc_delay = 22
vacc_cov = 0.7

if (!exists("YF2021_2022_savannah")) {
  cat("Loading the Savannah case data\n")
  load("YF2021_2022_savannah_date.RData")
} else {
  cat("Case data already loaded\n")
}

column = "DateOfOnset"

presenting_dates = YF2021_2022_savannah_date[[column]]

tab_all_dates <- function(x) {
  stopifnot(inherits(x, "Date"))
  
  # counts for dates that appear
  counts <- table(x)                 # names are "yyyy-mm-dd" as character
  counts <- as.integer(counts)
  names(counts) <- names(table(x))
  
  # full date range (includes dates not present)
  full <- seq(min(x, na.rm = TRUE), max(x, na.rm = TRUE), by = "day")
  out <- integer(length(full))
  names(out) <- as.character(full)
  
  # fill observed counts into the full vector
  out[names(counts)] <- counts
  
  out
}

d <- tab_all_dates(presenting_dates)

blank.count = 1

onset_data = c(rep(0, blank.count), d, rep(0, 365-length(d)-blank.count))

#Load TSI (temperature suitability index) components
load("savannah_TSI.RData")

# Data Manipulation
# 1. Convert the 'date' column to actual Date objects
# (Ensure the format matches your data, e.g., "%Y-%m-%d")
savannah_TSI$date <- as.Date(savannah_TSI$date)

# 2. Re-define the start date (now that the column is fixed)
start_date <- min(savannah_TSI$date)

# 3. NOW calculate the index
# This will now produce numbers (0, 31, 61...) instead of an error
savannah_TSI$time_idx <- as.numeric(savannah_TSI$date - start_date)

#Step function for temperature dependent parameters
# Ensure your data is sorted by date/time_idx
savannah_TSI <- savannah_TSI[order(savannah_TSI$time_idx), ]

# Create the step functions
# f = 0 means: "For any time t between 0 and 31, use the value at 0."
# rule = 2 means: "If t goes past the last date, just keep using the last value."

mu_step_fun <- approxfun(x = savannah_TSI$time_idx, 
                         y = savannah_TSI$mu, 
                         method = "constant", 
                         f = 0, 
                         rule = 2)

a_step_fun <- approxfun(x = savannah_TSI$time_idx, 
                        y = savannah_TSI$a, 
                        method = "constant", 
                        f = 0, 
                        rule = 2)

sigma_step_fun <- approxfun(x = savannah_TSI$time_idx, 
                            y = savannah_TSI$sigma_v,
                            method = "constant", 
                            f = 0, 
                            rule = 2)
```

# Weighted Resample
After the baseline run, we want to do a weighted resample, so do that here

```{r weighted-resample}
df_kept <- as.data.frame(res_kept, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# How many results to keep?
n <- lhs.scenario.sample.count

# Distribute the weights
w <- 1 / exp(df_kept$nll)
w <- w / sum(w)

# Do the sampling
sampled_idx <- sample.int(nrow(df_kept), size = n, replace = TRUE, prob = w)

# Parse out the results
sampled_kept <- df_kept[sampled_idx,]
params_10k <- sampled_kept[, c("rho", "Iv0", "v_mult")]
```
